chapter: Own bands and Los Angeles clubs
title: His Club Alabam band with Art Pepper and Nat Cole's arrangements
summary: At the Club Alabam Lee led a nine-piece integrated band with Art Pepper and Jack McVea, and Nat wrote pencil arrangements for $8 or $10 each.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: At which point ... had we covered that? You had the band at the Club Alabam?

No, I forgot about it -- but it was when after he was out here and he just had his trio, but that's when I had -- it was during the time I had Art Pepper, Jack MacVay and Luke Jones was playing saxaphones at the Club Alabam, and a trumpet player named Chiefie, and I guess it was Dudley.
But I don't know what time that was, because Art Pepper was very young, and you know Art Pepper, right?
Yeah, I know Art Pepper. Benny Carter told me he came west with him, and then he lost sight of him for a couple of years.
Well, he worked with me at the Club

Alabam, and he was a very young guy -- a very young guy. I mean, he was just as clean as he could be -- he had no problems then, you know? But I kind of did always integrate my bands; whatever it was.

And another fellow was making arrangements for me that I wanted to tell you about -- he turned out to be a big musician; I was paying him $10 an arrangement. I can't -- I see him sometimes -- his name on television now, but I don't remember.
But I can't get when that time was at the Alabam, you know? I stayed at the Alabam quite a while with the band, too.
How big a band was that?

That was like 3,6, we had 3 saxaphones, 3 brass; I think it was 9. There was 9, yeah. And we had to play for the shows; we had to play the dance music. But Nat used to arrange in pencil; he never did use a pen; he'd bring the arrangements in. Oh, and incidentally, yes, he used to do the arrangements for C.P. Johnson at the Rum Boogie.
See, all these places had shows, and I think that's where Nat made a lot of extra money during that time -- I'm talking about when you didn't pay but $8 or $10 for an arrangement.
The Bell Tavern? He used to write for the show
at the Bell Tavern, and he used to write for the Rum Boogie show.
But me, he would just make arrangements for my band, and he wrote in pencil. And I have some of the arrangements at home that Nat wrote, and his arrangements were quite good. Quite good.
